questions.0.explain.t: It decides who does what and in what sequence in a multi-agent flow.

questions.0.options.0.t: Several agents or steps, defining order, parallelism and context passing

questions.0.options.1.t: Only the training of the model and the tuning of its weights

questions.0.options.2.t: The printing of reports generated by the agent

questions.0.options.3.t: The compression of images sent to the model

questions.1.explain.t: One agent's output is the next one's input; trust should not be transitive.

questions.1.options.0.t: A compromised agent contaminating the others with instructions or data

questions.1.options.1.t: A lack of tokens available in the contracted plan

questions.1.options.2.t: The flow becoming too fast for users to follow

questions.1.options.3.t: Having too many comments in the orchestration code

questions.1.q.t: What is a risk in multi-agent systems?

questions.2.explain.t: Limits on steps, time and cost are basic safety brakes.

questions.2.options.0.t: To avoid infinite loops and runaway cost

questions.2.options.1.t: To make the model more creative on each attempt

questions.2.options.2.t: To increase the size of the available context

questions.2.options.3.t: To turn off the logs after a few rounds

questions.2.q.t: Why limit the number of iterations of an agent?
